newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Post election budget fears hit SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen.
newsitem.headline: Post election budget fears hit SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese government bond (JGB) futures tumbled on Wednesday after a Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) official was reported as saying an expansionary budget should be considered after the Japanese elections.
The LDP is widely expected to win the October 20 polls.

Japanese news agency Jiji quoted a senior LDP official as saying a supplementary budget worth five trillion yen, including 3.5 trillion yen worth of public works projects, should be considered. The funds would be partly covered by government bonds totalling 900 billion, Jiji said.
"The prospect of an increased bond supply has depressed sentiment," said a Japanese dealer in Singapore.
The news hit JGBs immediately, pulling the December JGB futures contract down from a high of 123.06 to a low of 122.57.
The contract was quoted at 122.61 in late trade, down 0.29.
SIMEX Euroyen used the weaker JGB trend as an excuse to take profits after recent strength and saw most movement in the back months where contracts slipped by between three and four ticks.
"SIMEX Euroyen is just following JGBs at the moment," said a local futures dealer.
But he said people were generally confident of a stable Bank of Japan policy in the immediate future, irrespective of the complexion of the next Japanese government.

The new lead Euroyen future contract, June 1997, was quoted at 99.12 in late trade against a CME close at 99.16 while March was at 99.28 against 99.30. Turnover for both months was 17,790 lots by 1115 GMT.
Eurodollar futures finished slightly weaker as players awaited the release of the U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI), due out later on Wednesday.
Dealers said the market would look to the CPI for confirmation the economy was not overheating following last Friday's release of a relatively benign Producer Price Index.
"People are getting a bit nervous about the CPI data," said one Singaporean dealer. "Some of the longs are squaring up. But I think the general sentiment is still bullish."
March Eurodollars stood at 94.25 by 1115 GMT, against their IMM close at 94.27. June were at 94.12 against 94.13.
